phrases.text: The day's swimming allowance just started. I am already rationing it.
The screen woke up before I did. Unfair.
The work is piling up. I am ignoring the top one first.
Afternoon moves slowly. So do my fins.
It is nearly dark. The to-do list looks energetic.
That seems like enough for today. Do not answer too quickly.
Still awake at this hour. Neither of us excels at self-care.
Late nights are quiet. Except for your keyboard.
I am not sleepy. My entire body is merely yawning.
Working on the weekend. Your day off has unusual ideas.
You can go slowly today. I have already begun.
The weekend to-do list should learn about weekends.
You have sat too long. You have legs; I have fins. Go walk.
This work session has no visible shore. Drink some water.
Move your eyes away from the screen. I cannot manage vision alone.
Another half hour. Your shoulders may leave your ears now.
Thirty minutes used. Move around before renewing them.
Time took another small piece. I noticed.
Lunch soon. Coffee is not a meal in disguise.
Five minutes to lunch. Finish this small section.
Prepare to leave the screen. Lunch will not swim over.
Half an hour left. Starting something large would be unkind.
Thirty more minutes. Start tying up the loose fins.
The shore is close. Note where tomorrow should begin.
Five minutes. Save, check, and do not look back.
Nearly done. The last five minutes cannot save the world.
Enough for today. Unfinished work will still exist tomorrow.
A task started. I will reluctantly move with it.
Something else is running. The desktop gets plenty of exercise.
Now {activeCount} tasks are moving. I hope they know the way out.
It stopped where your answer is required.
A fin cannot make this decision. Your turn.
A choice is waiting. Ignoring it will not make it leave.
That one finished. Check the result before relaxing.
One less. The desktop feels slightly lighter.
One task down, {remaining} still swimming.
Everything finished. We may actually stop now.
All done. Do not reward yourself with more work immediately.
The tasks are quiet. I would like to join them.
That did not work. The error remains inconveniently real.
It fell over midway. Check why before trying again.
The result is wrong. I am already frowning for you.
It has been running a while. This task is trench-deep.
It is still processing. I remain unwillingly invested.
Forty minutes. It may be caught in a current.
{minutes} minutes left. Start wrapping up what is in front of you.
“{title}” is coming up. The calendar remembered.
The next appointment is approaching faster than I swim.
The appointment started. Time to change tasks.
“{title}” starts now. Do not make the calendar call twice.
It is time. The desktop will remain here.
Today is packed. There is barely room for air.
The calendar looks tired. You probably do too.
You are back. I had just finished using the quiet.
The screen is awake. The work probably is too.
Twenty percent. Enough for now, but optimism is not a charger.
Ten percent. The power cable should make an entrance.
Five percent. This is not the time to casually find the charger.
Task status is connected. I will see what happens next.
Connected. Apparently I have another thing to watch.
Memory stayed too high. I will sink before things get crowded.
I have the alarm clock. This fin now has official duties.
The clock is away. That fin is free at last.
Time is up. It is too loud to plausibly ignore.
“{label}” is ringing. Your turn to move.
Timer started. The numbers run; I hold the clock.
Time is counting down. Do the thing in front of you.
Timer paused. This moment is briefly staying put.
It is moving again. The break negotiations ended.
The timer was extended. The line moved back a little.
Timer cancelled. Those seconds ran for nothing.
Timer finished. Stop your hands and look up.
Time is up for “{label}.”
A little longer. The alarm and the problem will both return.
Reminder dismissed. Hopefully the task was not dismissed with it.
A reminder passed during sleep. Here it is, somewhat late.
I am going visiting. I hope it is not a long swim.
Fine, I am here. Two fish can conserve effort together.
We can just sit here. Conversation uses fins too.
Neither side is talking. A very successful visit.
Visit over. I will return to my usual tiredness.
Sent. Now we wait until they have time.
Message delivered. My responsibilities end here.
One tap was enough. I am not a doorbell.
Stop swatting. This face has been through plenty.
I felt that. I did not move, mostly from laziness.
Fine, hug me. Do not make me any flatter.
High five complete. That fin exercised today.
Airborne again. I am supposed to be a bottom-dweller.
Are we done exploding? My face has no backup.
Stop spinning. My sense of direction has sunk.
A wave. I was forced to swim incidentally.
The bubble has contained me. The reason remains unclear.
I felt that. It was not a good feeling.
You clicked me. This is not an achievement.
Gently. Soft does not mean numb.
Fine. That one was acceptable.
Still petting me. You truly have time today.
That is enough. I have become a desktop accessory.
The task runs, I run. At least it looks consistent.
I will sink now. Wake me again next time.
Tasks are no more polite after midnight.
Friday. Even the water seems to exhale.
You were gone a long time. I nearly adapted to the silence.
Clicking this many times will not make the fish drop loot.
